icohp_lobster_v3.method: LOBSTER 5.1.1, all-PAW nscf nbnd500 ecut70/560 k222 pbeVaspFit2015; charge spilling 1.37% (<5% OK)
icohp_lobster_v3.icobi_interpretation: bond order: P-S 0.925 ~ 1 = covalent single bond (stiff PS4 framework, robust to Br). Li-S/Cl/Br 0.28-0.38 = low = IONIC. Li-Br(0.280) ~ Li-Cl(0.288) similar covalency -> Br bond weakening (ICOHP -1.93 vs -2.11) is IONIC in origin (bond elongation -> weaker electrostatic, matches Coulomb 4.34<4.70), NOT a covalency change. ICOHP(strength)+ICOBI(order) together: covalent framework + ionic Li-halide, Br softens the ionic bond.
icohp_lobster_v3.headline: Li-Br (-1.934) WEAKER than Li-Cl (-2.111) — Br weakens the Li-halide bond. Same-structure Cl-vs-Br direct comparison (no comp1 needed).
icohp_lobster_v3.three_descriptor_consistency: length (Li-Br 2.752 > Li-Cl 2.597), Coulomb q1q2/r (Li-Br 4.34 < Li-Cl 4.70), -ICOHP (Li-Br 1.934 < Li-Cl 2.111) ALL agree Li-Br weaker.
icohp_lobster_v3.dual_effect: P-S -5.913 = strong covalent (stiff PS4 framework, robust to Br; matches Bader 'Br strengthens PS4'). Li-halide weak/ionic, Br weakens further. Br dual: stiffens covalent framework + softens ionic Li-halide.
icohp_lobster_v3.narrative: Br -> weaker Li-halide -> softer lattice (lower modulus) + easier Li migration (lower Ea/higher sigma). ICOHP = bond-strength descriptor for the modulus story (slide panel v).
